subject: SOC 2 evidence: coverage for Dedicated pools + bridge letter / audit period
messages:
From: Joyce Patel <joyce.patel@greenlinebank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@greenlinebank.com
Date: Sun, 08 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 Type II + hosting coverage question

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Two quick asks as we move to procurement: can you confirm whether your SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period) covers GreenLine's use of Dedicated GPU pools when we elect reserved capacity? Specifically:

- Does the report include dedicated pools that are logically isolated per customer, or is it scoped only to the hosted multi-tenant runtime?
- If dedicated pools are out of scope, will Redwood provide a bridge letter or attestation that maps controls for dedicated pools for the audit period 2025-10-01 through 2026-03-31 (our procurement window)?

We need this to close our security review next week. If you have a redacted report or a draft bridge-letter template, please send.

Attachments requested: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted ok), proposed bridge letter, and any mapping/doc that explains coverage of Dedicated vs VPC/on-prem.

Thanks,
Joyce
Joyce Patel
Director, InfoSec Operations
GreenLine Bank
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Joyce Patel <joyce.patel@greenlinebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II + hosting coverage question

Hi Joyce — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: our SOC 2 Type II (period ending 2025-12-31) covers the hosted runtime and the shared control environment that underpins Dedicated pools, but there are important caveats for Dedicated and Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that your procurement team should be aware of.

Key points:
- Hosted (multi-tenant): fully in-scope for the 2025 Type II report.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): core control environment (identity, logging, patching, kernel-level infra controls) is covered when Redwood manages the pool in our data centers/cloud. However, tenant isolation architecture and customer-controlled network/VPC configuration are scoped differently; some customer-specific networking controls (e.g., customer-managed firewall rules, private peering) are not covered in our hosted Type II.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: generally out of scope for the standard Type II because the customer controls and environment are customer-managed. We support a bridge-letter pattern in those cases.

What we can provide immediately: a redacted copy of the 2025 SOC 2 Type II (attached), and a draft bridge letter that explains how our controls map to the SOC criteria for Dedicated pools and VPC deployments.

Questions for you to help us prepare the bridge-letter language:
1) Do you plan to use Redwood Dedicated where Redwood manages the pool (we provide the GPU hosts and manage patching/ops) or will you self-manage a private deployment in your VPC?
2) Is your procurement team looking for coverage that precisely matches 2025-10-01 through 2026-03-31 (we can produce a backfill note but need to confirm dates)?

I attached a redacted PDF and a bridge-letter draft. Marissa / Karthik — adding you for the draft bridge wording and to confirm the audit-period backfill approach.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
